paper.title_en: Nonlocality relates cuprate photoemission $ω/T$ scaling to a broad dielectric loss peak
paper.abstract_en: Photoemission spectroscopy on high $T_c$ cuprates reveals a puzzling nodal self-energy with $ω/T$ scaling and an exponent varying continuously with doping. Meanwhile, electron energy loss spectroscopy finds a broad $\sim 1$eV peak whose physical origin remains debated. We propose they share a common origin by introducing a phenomenological model of nonlocal screening in a many-body charged fluid. The model's key feature is spatially nonlocal effective repulsions between carriers $V_α(r) \sim 1/r^α$, with doping-dependent $α$. The model predicts a falsifiable relationship between independently measured self-energy exponent $γ$ and loss function peak dispersion exponent $α$, as $γ= 2-\frac{1}α$. This can be tested using modern ARPES and EELS. Nonlocality provides an alternative route to $ω/T$ scaling in observables, although it is conventionally regarded as a signature of quantum criticality.
